SREKAR REDDY 
SENIOR  DELIVERY  MANAGER  
US Client Delivery · Technical Staffing, SOW & Change Orders · Application, Web / Mobile & Cloud Delivery 
Hyderabad, India • +91 93915 87326 • Sre.pgmp@gmail.com • Immediate Joiner • Open to Night Shift (CST) 
P ROFESS  IONAL  S UM M ARY  
Senior Delivery Manager, 17 years in IT, from a software-engineering start into end-to-end delivery leadership 
for US and global clients. Own the US customer relationship directly and run technical delivery across 
application development, web/mobile, cloud, and managed -services engagements, while carrying the 
commercial side — SOWs, change orders, estimation, and proposals for new work. Build the staffing behind 
delivery as well: turning client requirements into staffing plans and technical job descriptions, screening and 
interviewing engineering candidates, and running technical evaluations that feed staffing and account 
decisions. An engineering background keeps the conversation with architects and leads real rather than 
administrative, and delivery stays predictable through disciplined governance and a steady monthly and 
quarterly reporting cadence with US stakeholders. Comfortable owning delivery on US (CST) night-shift hours. 
PMP, SAFe Agilist, CSM, CSPO, and ITIL certified. 
CORE  COM  P ETENCIES  
US Client & Account US Customer Relationship Ownership · Executive & Account-Manager Reporting · Monthly /

CERTIFICAT IONS  
PMP • SAFe® Agilist • Certified ScrumMaster (CSM) • Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO) • ITIL 
P ROFESS  IONAL  EX P ERIE  NCE  
Senior Delivery Manager | Tritech Software Solutions Sep 2021 – Present 
Technical delivery across US and global B2B engagements — Mercedes-Benz Financial Services (loan origination, 
payments, dealer, KYC) under a BOT GCC model, alongside life-sciences, pharma, and fintech accounts (Vertex, UCB 
Pharma, Drip Capital). Application development and managed-services delivery. 
DELIVERY & CUSTOMER MANAGEMENT 
• Lead end-to-end delivery across concurrent application-development and managed-services engagements, 
coordinating product, engineering, architecture, QA, and operations through the full SDLC. 
• Own the US client relationship as the primary delivery interface — status, technical delivery concerns, risks, 
escalations, priorities, execution decisions — with the monthly and quarterly status reviews that keep account 
managers and executives current. 
• Build the staffing behind delivery: turn client technical requirements into staffing plans and technical job 
descriptions, screen and interview engineering candidates, and run technical evaluations that feed staffing 
and account decisions. 
• Directly manage 4–5 project managers / scrum masters — delivery direction, coaching, performance 
management, and succession planning. 
• Own delivery planning across the engagements: resource and capacity planning, estimation, project initiation, 
execution planning, release readiness, and the Go/No-Go call. 
• Draft and manage SOWs and change orders. When scope moves, price its effort, capacity, schedule, and 
commercial impact and route it through a formal change order before it quietly becomes margin the team 
eats — and shape SOW and commercial terms at the pricing stage on new pursuits rather than inheriting 
whatever was signed. 
• Manage scope, change, risk, issue, and dependency across the engagements, and coordinate vendors and 
technology partners around delivery priorities and release commitments. 
IMPACT & OUTCOMES 
• Set up the delivery governance and reusable artefacts from scratch — templates, RAID cadence, reporting 
structures, review forums. None of it existed as a system before; now it does. 
• Delivery predictability went from 60% to 85%+, and on-time delivery holds at 95% — that came from planning 
and dependency discipline, not from pushing people harder. 
• Took a red account back to green in about eight weeks by rebuilding governance, resequencing intake, and 
having the nerve to stop work the team could not safely absorb. 
• Attrition on the teams dropped from 23% to 8% in a year through bi-weekly 1:1s that meant something and 
development plans people could see moving; promoted managers into larger delivery roles. 
• Own the delivery P&L — cost, utilization, forecasting, margin — held within about 5% of forecast, with 
roughly 8% taken out of delivery cost through capacity and vendor governance. 
COMMERCIAL & TECHNICAL DELIVERY 
• For Mercedes-Benz Financial Services, delivered the build fixed-price then moved the engagement onto a 
usage-linked production model tied to application-processing volume — revenue tracks what the client 
actually runs, and that credibility has driven renewals and scope expansion. 
• Coordinate delivery across enterprise web/mobile applications, cloud-based solutions, IoT, and other 
platforms, keeping enough technical depth to challenge assumptions, spot delivery risks early, and 
communicate credibly with engineering leadership. 
Technical Delivery Manager | Deloitte USI Jul 2017 – Sep 2021 
Enterprise application, web / mobile, and managed-services delivery for US, UK, and Middle-East clients, with 
distributed teams across India, Ukraine, and the US. Fixed-bid and T&M, in banking, capital markets, financial services, 
and healthcare. 
APPLICATION & TECHNICAL DELIVERY 
• Led concurrent greenfield web and mobile application-development programs from inception to production 
for US customers, under fixed-bid and T&M, working directly with US client leadership on priorities, risks, 
dependencies, and escalations across the India–US–Ukraine spread. 
• Managed 2–3 project managers / scrum masters across concurrent engineering programs — delivery 
oversight, mentoring, capability development — and worked with solution and enterprise architects and 
product stakeholders on technical constraints, integration risks, and delivery dependencies. 
• Built an IoT indoor-navigation product for a global US client (Bluetooth beacons to smartphones for precise 
indoor positioning, web and mobile kept in sync) and an ML-based parking-availability forecasting product for 
a major US client. 
STAFFING, SOW & PROPOSALS 
• Led firm-level technology hiring beyond my own portfolio — screening and interviewing engineering 
candidates and building the hiring and evaluation capability the delivery org ran on. 
• Prepared SOWs, effort estimates, staffing requirements, blended-rate models, budgets, and forecasts for 
existing and new engagements, and ran resource and capacity planning — staffing to demand ahead of the 
cycle, managing bench and billable utilization. 
• Partnered with sales and business development on RFP analysis, technical feasibility, solutioning, and delivery 
proposals for new work, and assessed feasibility before commitments so scope matched real capability and 
capacity. 
MANAGED SERVICES & GOVERNANCE 
• Grew a managed-services estate from 5 to 50+ applications by turning recurring incidents and improvement 
asks into scoped engineering work and fresh SOWs; moved L3 support onto Kanban and ran release 
management and business-continuity / disaster-recovery testing with global stakeholders. 
• Stood the delivery governance up from a blank page — delivery-health reviews, RAID cadence, release 
governance, capacity planning, executive reporting — and ran SAFe governance across 7–8 teams where 
predictability climbed from the low 60s into the mid-80s. 
• Grew 7–8 project managers, scrum masters, and technical leads into independent ownership over 12–18 
months, and mentored six new scrum masters. 
Recognition: Outstanding Delivery Leader of the Year · Best Mentor of the Year 
Project Manager / Agile Coach | Altruista Health (UnitedHealth Group) Aug 2016 – Jul 2017 
Delivery of enterprise healthcare and payer platforms across US–India teams — preventive care, member engagement, 
and care-gap visibility in a regulated payer environment. 
• Ran delivery across development, QA, and database functions, owning roadmap planning, sprint planning, 
dependencies, and release readiness, working straight with US product leadership to turn priorities into 
commitments and executable roadmaps. 
• When the Agile coach left mid-transformation, picked up the coaching role alongside the delivery role and 
moved 25+ teams onto Agile without letting delivery slide. 
Project Manager / Delivery Lead | SP Software (CallHealth) Mar 2015 – Jun 2016 
End-to-end delivery of one of India's early integrated digital-health platforms — virtual consultation, diagnostics, home 
care, pharmacy, and health-plan modules — from the founder's first product sessions through production. 
• In the room with the founder and CXO from the first product sessions, turning market read and service design 
into scope engineering could build — startup pace, judgement over process because the process didn't exist 
yet. 
• Carried it the whole way: requirements, functional spec, delivery, production launch, and the enhancements 
after. 
Senior Business Analyst & BA Practice Lead | Avenir IT Apr 2014 – Feb 2015 
• Set up the BA practice and led QA for a UK hedge-fund platform — requirements, traceability, and workflow 
across front, middle, and back office, wired into Bloomberg and Reuters across equities and FX under tight 
compliance. 
• Walked into a stalled engagement built on requirement gaps and got delivery moving again. 
Software Engineer → Project Manager | Digimatrix Technologies Sep 2008 – Mar 2014 
Enterprise and US public-sector software delivery in banking, capital markets, and healthcare — regulated work with 
real change control, traceability, and multi-vendor coordination. 
• Started as a Java / J2EE engineer on Spring and Oracle, building enterprise and US public-sector applications, 
before moving into full delivery ownership  — the engineering grounding that lets delivery and technical risk 
be read clearly rather than taken at face value from a status update. 
• Ran delivery across concurrent programs: requirements, implementation planning, releases, milestones, 
dependencies, and stakeholder communication. 
TECH  N O LOG Y & TOOLS  
Engineering: Java / J2EE · Spring · Oracle · SQL · REST / APIs · Web & Mobile Applications 
Exposure: Cloud (AWS / Azure) · IoT · Machine Learning 
Delivery: Jira · Azure DevOps · Confluence · Power BI · MS Project · SAFe · Scrum · Kanban · Hybrid SDLC
